problem:
What type of quadratic curve is defined by the following equation?

$$
{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}^{2}-4{x}_{2}=0
$$

feedback.problem:
What type of quadratic curve is defined by the following equation?

$$
{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}=-5
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we complete the squares for the variable ${x}_{1}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1} & =-5 \\ ({x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}+4)-4 & =-5 \\ ({x}_{1}-2)^{2} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, performing the change of variable

$$
{y}_{1}={x}_{1}-2,\,
$$

we get the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}^{2} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

 
which defines an empty set. Notice that the left-hand side is non-negative for all ${y}_{1}$ while the right-hand side is negative. In this case, we say that the equation represents a pair of imaginary parallel lines.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: A pair of imaginary parallel lines
